subject: Re: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)
body:
From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 4:18 PM
Subject: Fwd: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)

Aisha — escalating per your note from last week.

Heliotrope is pushing for audit logging commitments to be explicit in the MSA Exhibit (coverage + evidence expectations). They’re holding signature until we respond to their redline.

Key asks in their redline (see attached):
- “100% coverage of all administrative and privileged actions” across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- audit log availability/export: “real-time” and “no later than 1 minute.”
- “immutable/tamper-proof” language.
- evidence: “provide audit log samples and control evidence on request within 5 business days.”

Can you + Marcus + Olga give a sign-off on what we can commit to? Legal can draft, but they want Security/GRC to confirm we won’t over-commit.

Attachment: HB_Redwood_MSA_ExhibitD_AuditLogging_v3_REDLINE.docx

—
Sofia Mendes
Contract Language Alignment (Audit/Retention)
Redwood Inference

From: Jenna Collins <jenna.collins@heliotropebank.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA Exhibit D — Audit Logging
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliotropebank.com>, Outside Counsel (Heliotrope) <vendorcontracts@outsidecounsel-hb.com>

Sofia,

Thanks — attaching updated redline. Our security team requires contractual commitments around audit log completeness and delivery timelines, plus an evidence turn-around expectation.

Please confirm Redwood can:
1) Log all administrative/privileged actions that impact access/security/configuration/billing/availability.
2) Deliver audit logs for export within 60 seconds of the action.
3) Provide evidence (sample logs + control documentation) within 5 business days upon request.

Best,
Jenna

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 5:02 PM
Subject: Re: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)

Marcus / Olga — need quick guidance tonight.

We should not sign “100% of all admin/privileged actions” in a generic way. We can commit to:
- logging defined “Sensitive Actions” (access/RBAC/API keys, deployments/rollouts, routing/quota/capacity changes, retention/export config), and
- maintaining a versioned schema + inventory, with enforcement (CI + coverage dashboard), and
- delivering logs with an SLO (not “real-time” / 60 seconds hard guarantee).

Questions for sign-off:
1) Delivery lag: what SLO are we comfortable putting in writing for enterprise (e.g., 99% <= 5 minutes, 99.9% <= 15 minutes)?
2) “Tamper-proof/immutable”: can we say “append-only storage with access controls and integrity safeguards” (no absolute guarantees), and “customers can export to their own immutable store”?
3) Evidence SLA: can we commit to 10 business days instead of 5? What is realistic for GRC without derailing other audits?

If you can send a proposed stance + wording bullets, I’ll route back to Sofia/Legal.

— Aisha
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 6:11 PM
Subject: Re: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)

Agree we should avoid “all admin actions” + “100% coverage” as a blanket warranty.

Security recommendation (what’s true + defensible):

Coverage language
- Define “Sensitive Actions” as actions that materially impact customer data access, security posture, billing, or availability.
- Commit to: “Redwood will generate audit log events for Sensitive Actions initiated via Redwood systems,” with an explicit list of categories.
- Do NOT commit that every conceivable privileged action is covered in perpetuity; instead: “Redwood maintains an internal inventory of Sensitive Actions and audits instrumentation coverage; Customer may request the current list.”

Delivery language
- SLO we can stand behind: “99% of audit events available for query/export within 5 minutes,” excluding third-party sink unavailability.
- We should explicitly allow short delays due to retries/backpressure. Hard 60 seconds is not realistic during exporter backlogs.

Integrity / tamper
- Avoid “tamper-proof.” Suggest: “Audit logs are stored in an append-only system with restricted access controls and monitored access. Redwood maintains controls to detect and investigate unauthorized modification.”
- Also okay to say: “Customers can export logs to a customer-controlled destination (e.g., S3/SIEM) for long-term retention/immutability.”

If Olga aligns on evidence SLA, I’m comfortable signing this posture.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, Jul 2, 2025 at 7:04 PM
Subject: Re: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)

+1 to Marcus’s framing.

On evidence expectations:
- I strongly prefer we avoid a hard “5 business days” commitment in the MSA. It’s often feasible but not always (auditor fieldwork weeks, concurrent enterprise requests).
- Proposed: “within ten (10) business days, or as otherwise mutually agreed,” and clarify scope: reasonable excerpts (sample events, control descriptions) rather than “all documentation.”

For SOC 2-style evidence, we can confidently offer:
- a schema description + field list,
- sample audit events (redacted),
- description of access controls for internal audit log access,
- and (if requested) a statement of how we map audit logging to our controls.

I can provide a one-page excerpt for Heliotrope (attached) that’s auditor-friendly without promising beyond our control environment.

Attachment: Redwood_Audit_Logging_Controls_SOC2_Mapping_Excerpt.pdf

— Olga
Olga Petrov
GRC Director
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 3, 2025 at 9:22 AM
Subject: Re: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)

Based on the above, here’s a contract-safe approach we can slot into Exhibit D (summary; I’ll work with Sofia to apply to the redline):

1) Coverage.
- Replace “100% of all administrative and privileged actions” with:
  “Redwood will generate audit logs for Sensitive Actions (defined as actions that materially impact Customer’s access controls, security configuration, billing, or service availability) performed within the Service.”
- Add: “Redwood maintains a versioned audit event schema and internal inventory of Sensitive Actions; upon request Redwood will provide Customer with the current list of audited event categories and representative event names.”

2) Delivery.
- Replace “real time / within 60 seconds” with:
  “Redwood will make audit log events available for query and export with a target service level objective of 99% of events within five (5) minutes.”
- Add carve-out for third-party sink unavailability and force majeure.

3) Integrity.
- Replace “tamper-proof/immutable” with:
  “Audit logs are stored in an append-only system with restricted access controls and monitoring. Customer may export audit logs to a Customer-controlled system for long-term retention and integrity controls.”

4) Evidence.
- Add: “Within ten (10) business days of a written request, Redwood will provide reasonable audit logging documentation and/or redacted sample events sufficient to support Customer’s compliance obligations.”

Aisha: please confirm you’re comfortable being listed as the internal approval for this posture (in case they ask for exec confirmation).

— Michael
Michael Grant
Legal (Privacy/Commercial)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Heliotrope Bank — Audit logging contract language (evidence + coverage commitments)

Sofia — approved to proceed with Michael’s proposed language.

Two specific notes to preserve in the redline:
- We should use our internal term “Sensitive Actions” (not “all admin actions”) and keep the “material impact” qualifier. This aligns with how the program is implemented and audited.
- Delivery should be SLO-based (99% within 5 minutes). Do not accept a hard 60-second commitment.

Olga’s evidence excerpt is fine to share as supporting material (not as a contractual attachment).

If Heliotrope requests an executive statement: you can state that Security Engineering + GRC + Legal have reviewed and that I’ve signed off on the posture.

— Aisha
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
Redwood Inference
